clusters.headline: Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya
clusters.summary: The Swiss government told the BBC that the freed national was on her way back to Switzerland.

clusters.headline: Zimbabwe: Mnangagwa, Angel Caught Up in Another Al Jazeera Investigation That Reveals Zimbabwean Govt Paid UK Terrorist Groups to Force Lifting of Sanctions
clusters.summary: [New Zimbabwe] President Emmerson Mnangagwa's advisor Uebert Angel has been caught up in another Al Jazeera investigation that reveals as much as US$13,000 was paid for a fake rally on the sidelines of COP26, seeking to portray British people's support for a UK-Zimbabwe relationship.

clusters.headline: Africa: Africa CDC and Ethiopian Airlines Partner to Offer 20% Airfare Discount to Self-Sponsored CPHIA 2026 Participants
clusters.summary: [Africa CDC] The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and Ethiopian Airlines have partnered to offer a 20% discount on air tickets to participants attending the Fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) who are funding their own participation.

clusters.headline: South Africa: Black Market Weight-Loss Drug Sellers Are Moving Fast. South Africa's Regulators Are Struggling To Keep Up
clusters.summary: [Bhekisisa] South African regulators have won an important court battle against a pharmacy making its own versions of popular weight-loss injections. clusters.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
clusters.summary: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

clusters.headline: South Africa: Bronkhorstspruit Water Crisis Exposes a National Pattern of Municipal Failure and Impunity
clusters.summary: [Daily Maverick] The Bronkhorstspruit water crisis, which has sickened about 450 people, exposes deep-rooted failures in local government, poor oversight and a culture of non-accountability that puts public health at risk. clusters.headline: Zimbabwe: 200,000 Zimbabweans Have So Far Fled South Africa's Anti-Migrant Protests - Cabinet Told
clusters.summary: [New Zimbabwe] Just under 200,000 Zimbabweans have so far fled South Africa's anti-migrant protests, according to the government.

clusters.headline: Singapore’s Toh Wei Soong bags silver in 100m backstroke S7, his 4th medal at Asian Para Games
clusters.summary: Toh now has a total of four medals at the Games this year, but no gold.

clusters.headline: Teen arrested over axe attack on Sarawak teacher; minister urges public not to shame student
clusters.summary: "This matter must be approached with care and compassion. The adolescent involved is still growing and developing," said Sarawak's Minister of Women, Children and Community Well-being Development Fatimah Abdullah.

clusters.headline: Israel frees dozens of Americans, including U.S. Congress nominee, after West Bank detention
clusters.summary: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander along with dozens of American and Israeli rabbis and activists were helping Palestinian olive harvesters when they were detained by Israeli forces.

clusters.headline: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'
clusters.summary: The discovery of 12 women's bodies near Johannesburg has again highlighted South Africa's problem with violence against women.

clusters.headline: Mourners killed by Kenya police at Odinga national farewell not part of violence, BBC finds
clusters.summary: After analysing 1,500 videos and images of the Raila Odinga memorial, Africa Eye finds that those killed were far from the scuffles.
